glossary.definition: The process’s virtual-address context. Similar pointer values in different processes do not automatically refer to the same shared object. Mapping and ownership determine what the bytes mean.

A requirement on where an object can be placed in storage. Requested alignment can affect object size and layout. A sixty-four-byte alignment request is not a universal statement about every processor’s cache-line geometry.
Indivisibility of the specified operation on the relevant atomic object. It does not make several fields one transaction or retain the lifetime of a pointed-to object.
A policy that limits admission or slows producers when downstream capacity is unavailable. Blocking, rejection, and timed admission have different caller-visible contracts.

Access to an object or resource without owning its lifetime. A span, string view, raw pointer, or native descriptor argument can be a borrow. Validity depends on the owner’s lifetime and mutation rules.
A request or protocol that permits unfinished work to stop. It is not necessarily immediate, does not automatically wake every blocking API, and does not roll back external effects already performed.
A descriptor policy controlling whether the descriptor survives a successful process-image replacement. Acquisition-time flags avoid a race between resource creation and later flag assignment.
The protected state expression that determines whether a waiting participant may proceed. A notification is a wakeup mechanism, not the state or a reserved task.
A coherent operation on protected shared state. Its correct extent follows the invariant, not simply the desire to minimize the number of locked lines.
An absolute end time for the defined operation. Recreating a timeout after every partial transfer changes the contract from a total budget to a different waiting policy.

A process-local integer reference to an open resource. Copying the integer is not ownership duplication. Duplicating through the native API can create another descriptor referring to the same open file description.
A promise about persistence under a stated failure model. A successful write, close, unmap, or local in-memory commit does not automatically establish every desired crash-recovery property.

A termination observation whose meaning depends on the interface and protocol phase. A stream EOF inside a frame is truncation; a zero-length UDP datagram is a legitimate datagram, not stream closure.
The rule that identifies message boundaries within transported bytes. A length prefix, delimiter protocol, or fixed-size record must define bounds, invalid input, and truncated termination.

A language-level ordering relationship used to reason about visibility and the absence of conflicting unsynchronized accesses. A wall-clock guess or sleep is not a substitute for the required relationship.
A property or protocol under which repeating an operation has an appropriately controlled effect. It matters when a transport failure leaves the caller uncertain whether remote work already occurred.
A condition that must hold at the public observation boundaries of a component. Locks protect access, while validation and mutation order preserve logical validity.
Completion synchronization with a represented thread. It also establishes the point after which objects used only by that thread can be reclaimed under the surrounding ownership design.
A virtual-memory association with an underlying object or anonymous storage. Mapped bytes still require valid object interpretation, extent checks, and a stability policy for external mutation.
Kernel-managed open state that can be shared by duplicated descriptors, including an offset where relevant. Per-descriptor flags are a different layer.
A successful operation that completed only part of the requested transfer. The accepted prefix must be retained in the state machine; replaying from the start can duplicate effects.
A synchronization protocol that makes prepared data available to another participant. Reusing the storage often needs a reverse ownership handoff after the consumer finishes.
A state in which the relevant participants have stopped accessing an object. Joined shutdown supplies a useful quiescent boundary for resource cleanup and final accounting.
Associating resource ownership with object lifetime. Correct acquisition, move semantics, release behavior, and declaration order are essential parts of the pattern.
Collecting a terminated child process’s result through the platform’s process-wait mechanism. A numeric PID stored in a C++ variable does not perform this responsibility automatically.

A program execution outside the language’s prescribed requirements, for which the standard imposes no normal semantic guarantee. Passing tests does not legitimize an invalid lifetime, overflow, or data race.
